# Deviload 2.12.0

**Devil Music in liquid glass.** The player, its panels and its windows move smoothly, and the lyrics now follow you everywhere.

- The play button is a glass orb that breathes with the bass, the timeline fills like a glass tube with bubbles drifting through it, and the volume is the same tube. The mini-player gets all of it too.
- Panels, windows and menus glide open and shut. A new song flows into the player bar, the player's colour follows the new cover, and an album opened from a card takes its cover with it.
- One Lyrics button shows the words wherever the player is. In the full player the lines move in and out of focus, the music video can show them like subtitles, a floating strip keeps them on your desktop, and Share a line makes a picture of up to four lines to copy or save.
- Your listening week, month and year open in a stats window with your top artists and songs.

### Devil Music

Search puts the original song ahead of live takes, covers and remixes you did not ask for, keeps earlier results while you type and can be browsed with the arrow keys. Hovering the timeline shows the time and the line sung there; the mouse wheel seeks over the timeline and changes the volume over the speaker.

The phone remote and Listen together are redesigned, and the remote shows a sharp cover and the current line. Pausing when another app plays sound and levelling the loudness between songs are new options in playback settings, both off by default.

Choose Only Devil Music in the installer or in music settings to open straight into music; updates and your library stay the same. A short glass tour introduces the player on the first start.

Scrolling stays smooth while music plays, searches and the side panels no longer stall, and the window moves and resizes without the interface lagging behind. Lyrics stay in step with what you hear.

### Deviload

The download queue is checked less often while nothing is downloading, and the Deviload tour uses the same glass style.

On Windows, run the setup EXE over your installed copy to keep your library and settings. Deleting your playlists and app data is only an option in the uninstaller and is off by default.
